issues_not_shipped.disposition: Docs-only in 5.0.1, plus contract tests and a 'Clarified' CHANGELOG line making the 7–8 digit body range explicit. `minBodyLength` is rejected for 5.x. calculateVerifier `allowShortBody` is not planned. Choosing SII reception and emission floors is left to dte-sdk. Close as answered.
issues_not_shipped.reason: `minBodyLength` is a relaxation flag on validate() and isValidRut(), so it would brand short values as `Rut`. On decompose() it would relax the shared lenient core ('Folio 77' parses as a RUT), make compact shapes ambiguous, and break mask()'s anti-PII arithmetic (a 5-digit body would show 4 of its 5 digits). It is not tree-shakeable (about 100–140 B). SII's own floors disagree (XSD none, Reclamo WS reportedly 1000, Formato DTE 'entre 100.000 y 99 millones'), so rut.ts cannot encode 'the SII rule'. An allowShortBody option on calculateVerifier would break the tested coherence law that any body calculateVerifier accepts produces a validate()-passing RUT, and userland Modulo 11 is about 8 lines.

strategies.case_against_one_minor_per_issue: One minor per issue assumes every issue should add API. After review, only #47 survives as API. #44, #45 and #48 are knowledge, and #46 is not ready to freeze. Five minors (5.1–5.5) would mean five release PRs, five GitHub Releases, five www-rut.ts syncs and five changelog entries, a pattern that recalls the 2026-01-23 burst (3.0.0–3.4.0 in about 50 minutes) that already cost credibility. The version number alone would contradict the 'contract frozen' message. Sequential minors also let arrival order decide the size budget. The headroom is 192 B ESM / 186 B CJS, so whichever feature merges first takes it: #44's API at +108/+119 B would leave 67 B on CJS and decide #45, #46 and #47 by budget instead of merit. Most important under the freeze, naming and option vocabulary would be fixed one release at a time. Each export would freeze before the next one is designed, so inconsistencies (RUT_PATTERN vs SII_RUT vs an unnamed threshold, `validate` vs `requireValid` as option names, Spanish 'juridica' vs English format values) could never be fixed. The interactions also have to be decided together: kindOf vs generic RUTs, an extract strict option vs placeholders, shared grammar fragments between patterns and extract, and minBodyLength vs the frozen pattern strings.
strategies.case_against_single_big_release: It does not fit, and it freezes too much at once. Measured and estimated costs: #46 +178/+183 B, #44 API +108/+119 B, #45 +89 B, #47 about +50–80 B. That totals about 425–470 B against 192/186 B of headroom, so the caps would have to rise by about 25%, which undoes the 'tiny' positioning, or the work would move to subpaths that are frozen surface too. One tag would freeze five designs, and the per-issue challenges show three of them have wrong or unsourced data (holder-type ranges, an open placeholder list, a heuristic scanning grammar). There is no prerelease channel to catch mistakes, and a rollback needs a v6 the project has said it will not do. Review and Stryker work would come as one large batch, a defect in any part would block all of it, and the CHANGELOG would become a wall of text that readers skim past, which is the opposite of the clarity a frozen contract needs. It would also hold back urgent, zero-risk material (the clean() embedded-text correction, the policy clarifications, and four months of unpublished canary changes) until the slowest and riskiest item (#46) is done.
cross_issue_decisions_needed_first: Before 5.0.1: close the validate()/isValidRut() option set for 5.x. `strict?: boolean` is the only option, its type is never widened, and no allowance or minimum-length flags will be added. This one decision settles #44's allowance (both forms) and #48's minBodyLength, and it should be written as a 'Clarified' line in 5.0.1.

Before 5.0.1: make the body range 1.000.000–99.999.999 (7–8 digits, no leading zero) an explicit part of the frozen acceptance contract. It decides #48, and it fixes the floor that #47's pattern strings, any future #46 grammar and #45's ranges must follow.

Before 5.0.1: set the rut.ts vs dte-sdk boundary. rut.ts documents SII facts as reference; dte-sdk encodes them (SII_RUT 60803000-K, generic-receiver constants, RUTRecep '0', the 135 UF rule, the XSD RUTType pattern, reception and emission floors). 60803000-K is never called a placeholder.

Before 5.1.0: set the admission bar for post-freeze exports. (a) An export that only re-expresses an already-frozen contract (zero new semantics, e.g. RUT_PATTERNS) can ship on the maintainer's judgment with an equivalence proof. (b) An export that encodes data or heuristics owned by outside bodies (SII lists, Registro Civil ranges, text-scanning grammar) ships only on demand from outside arrowsw, after incubation, and never in core. Demand from dte-sdk alone does not qualify. This generalises the #36 parse() precedent.

Before 5.1.0: set the size-budget policy. Keep the 1.9 kB ESM / 2 kB CJS caps. Reserve at least about 100 B of headroom on each entry for future fixes. Anything that does not fit goes to a subpath with its own size-limit entry, or does not ship. Also decide whether 5.x will accept subpaths at all, since each exports-map entry is frozen once published.
Before 5.1.0: adopt the naming and option-vocabulary rules (below), because RUT_PATTERNS sets the precedent for every later constant and option.

Before any heuristic feature: choose the incubation venue. publish.yml publishes any v* tag with plain `npm publish` and has no dist-tag handling, so 'ship a beta and adjust' is not available in rut.ts. Incubate in dte-sdk (0.x), or add a `next` dist-tag path to publish.yml and RELEASING.md first.

Issue hygiene: close #44 and #48 when 5.0.1 ships, each with a comment stating what would reopen it. Close #45 (kindOf not planned; generate kind only on outside demand). Keep #46 open with a needs-demand label. Bring #36's parse() into the same demand-gated backlog so there is a single rule.
naming_and_consistency_rules: Exported data constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE with a `RUT_` prefix and a plural noun for a keyed collection, so #47 ships as `RUT_PATTERNS` (not `RUT_PATTERN`). There are no free-floating domain constants (no `SII_RUT`, no exported 50M threshold).

Constants are plain object literals with `as const` (readonly literal types), not Object.freeze, so they tree-shake in Rollup and esbuild. No separate exported type for a constant; consumers use `typeof RUT_PATTERNS`.

Reuse the existing shape vocabulary exactly: 'compact' | 'hyphen' | 'dotted' (as in GenerateFormat), plus `any` only where a union is needed. No synonyms such as 'dash', 'canonical', 'plain' or 'sii'.

Functions are camelCase and start with a verb. Predicates are `is*`, accept `unknown`, return boolean and never throw. Text scanning uses find*/scan*, never `extract`, which the docs already use for getBody/getVerifier.

Options are flat object types. Never widen the type of an existing option (`strict` stays `boolean`). Boolean options name the positive guarantee and reuse existing names: `requireValid` (the equals() precedent) for any validity toggle. Never name an option after an exported function (no `validate: boolean`). Never forward `strict` into new helpers; callers filter output with validate(x, { strict: true }) instead.
No numeric or enum knobs that make the canonical gate configurable (no minBodyLength). Enum values are in English only (e.g. 'natural' | 'legal' if holder kinds ever ship, never 'juridica').
Any RUT string returned by a new API is clean()'s compact form with an uppercase K, typed `string`. Only isValidRut() mints the branded `Rut`.

Errors: no new error classes (no RangeError). Helpers typed `string` follow the throwOnError-default-true convention with InvalidRutError and the constant message 'Invalid RUT input'. Helpers typed `unknown` return false, null or [] as appropriate. Nothing echoes input.
Every exported string or regex is frozen byte for byte, and its CHANGELOG entry says so. Exported pattern strings are backslash-free and stay within the JSON Schema interoperable regex subset.
Subpath names, if they are ever allowed, are domain nouns (`rut.ts/text`). There is no `rut.ts/sii`, because SII/DTE knowledge belongs in dte-sdk.
Changelog categories: 'Clarified' for documentation-level contract statements, 'Added' for exports, 'Internal' for CI/tooling. Never edit a released entry.
risks: Docs could publish wrong SII facts. Research reached sii.cl only through search snippets and a third-party, probably LLM-authored, transcription. Mitigation: the 5.0.1 gate requires the maintainer to have read every cited SII document, and unverifiable rows are dropped. Docs remain correctable, unlike exports.

Perception against the 'best library in Chile' goal: a plan that ships mostly docs can look like stagnation next to @rut-toolkit's feature breadth. Mitigation: present rut.ts on trust and DTE correctness (non-echoing errors, canonical gate, the SII special-RUT section that competitors get wrong by rejecting 66.666.666-6), publish the demand-gated backlog as a roadmap, and treat Spanish docs and migration guides from rut.js / @fdograph/rut-utilities (about 36K weekly downloads on unmaintained libraries) as the main adoption lever.

Drift between dte-sdk incubation and a later upstream: if dte-sdk's scanner or constants become the de facto spec, upstreaming will lock in whatever dte-sdk did. Mitigation: build the incubated code in dte-sdk as a self-contained, rut.ts-style module with the same test discipline (equivalence/property tests, no echo), and upstream it unchanged or not at all.

RUT_PATTERNS is permanent: a wrong character can only be fixed in v6. Mitigation: exhaustive and per-shape equivalence tests in CI, a 7-day public review of the exact strings, and leaving validate() internals untouched in the same release.

Misuse of the patterns: `any`/`compact` match every 9-digit Chilean mobile number, and pattern-only schemas (Zod toJSONSchema drops .refine) will accept them. Engine differences (trailing newline in Python/PHP/Java, case-insensitive engines admitting U+212A, MySQL _ci collations) can turn a 'shape hint' into a weaker gate than users expect. Mitigation: the README steers API schemas to hyphen/dotted and documents per-engine caveats.

Size budget erosion: CJS headroom (186 B) is tighter than ESM, and #47's cost is only a crude estimate (+50–80 B), not yet measured with terser. Without a reserved floor, a future security fix might not fit under the caps. Mitigation: keep about 100 B of headroom per entry as a release gate.

Making the body range explicit closes #48 option (2) for the rest of 5.x, and archival users (property registries, notaries, pensions) with real sub-1M RUNs must handle those rows outside rut.ts. This is intended, but the issue-closure comment and the README must say so plainly.

Demand from outside arrowsw may never appear (rut.ts has about 228 weekly downloads and every open issue is maintainer-filed), so the backlog may stay parked indefinitely. That is acceptable under the freeze, but the owner should accept it explicitly rather than let the backlog drift.

Release mechanics: publish.yml publishes any v* tag with plain `npm publish` and has no dist-tag handling. Anyone attempting an 'incubation beta' inside rut.ts would hit npm's prerelease tagging rules (refusal, or a release to all users on `latest`). Mitigation: add dist-tag handling first, or incubate only in dte-sdk.

Docs-only patch fatigue: a 5.0.1 followed shortly by a 5.1.0 means two www-rut.ts syncs. Mitigation: put every pending docs item into 5.0.1. If #47's gates are met in the same week, it is acceptable to merge both into a single 5.1.0, but docs must not wait on #47.
strategies.bottom_line: Do neither. Ship two releases and freeze only one new identifier. 5.0.1 (docs-only, runtime byte-identical, soon) answers #48 and #44, fixes the clean()-on-free-text advice behind #46, adds the generate() PII note from #45, writes 'validate options are closed for 5.x' and 'the 7–8 digit body is contract' as Clarified commitments, and publishes the canary changes held since July. 5.1.0 adds only #47's RUT_PATTERNS: backslash-free strings proven equivalent to the already-frozen isRutLike, with no Object.freeze and no internal refactor, measured within the existing caps with at least about 100 B left, after a 7-day public review of the exact strings. Reject the validate() allowance (#44), kindOf() (#45) and minBodyLength (#48) for 5.x. Defer GENERIC_RUTS, generate({kind}) and the free-text scanner (as a future rut.ts/text subpath) until demand comes from outside arrowsw, and incubate them in dte-sdk, which can change freely at 0.x. Settle the boundary policy, the admission bar, the size floor and the naming rules before 5.0.1 and 5.1.0 respectively, so the one export that does freeze sets the right precedent.

strategies.lens: Adopter and market view. The question is what makes Chilean developers choose rut.ts and trust it: a stable contract, accurate docs, a small bundle, and being findable in Spanish. Three facts shape the answer. First, rut.ts gets about 228 downloads a week, while two unmaintained libraries (rut.js and @fdograph/rut-utilities) get about 36K a week between them. Second, the release history has been bursty: npm shows 3.0.0 through 3.4.0 published between 21:09 and 22:00 UTC on 2026-01-23, and three majors in 2026 alone (3.0 on Jan 23, 4.0 on May 17, 5.0 on Jul 6). The 5.0.0 "contract freezes" promise is 113 days old, and nothing has been published since. Third, every ^5 range picks up each minor automatically. That includes CJS consumers, who get no tree-shaking and so pay for every added byte. Under this view a release is a trust signal and a marketing moment, not just a way to ship code.

contents: #47 only: RUT_PATTERN { any, compact, hyphen, dotted }. Anchored, flagless strings with no backslashes, using a [1-9] lead digit, [0-9] and [.]. Proven equal to isRutLike() after JS trim. any = '^([1-9][0-9]{6,7}-?[0-9kK]|[1-9][0-9]?[.][0-9]{3}[.][0-9]{3}-[0-9kK])$'.

Leave validate() internals untouched: no refactor that compiles validate from the pattern, and the leading-zero guard stays.

Add a README section 'Schema patterns (JSON Schema / OpenAPI / SQL / Zod)':

  - Prefer hyphen or dotted for API fields, because any and compact match every 9-digit mobile number.
  - Zod snippet: .trim().regex(new RegExp(RUT_PATTERN.any)).refine(validate), and pass { io: 'input' } to toJSONSchema when a transform follows.
  - Equivalence with validate() holds for JS trim only.
  - Engine notes: Python fullmatch, PHP /D, Ruby \A\z, strip the anchors for XSD, MySQL _ci collations.

strategies.case_against_one_minor_per_issue:
- **It repeats the churn pattern.** Five minors driven by five maintainer-authored issues filed on the same day would repeat the 2026-01-23 burst (3.0.0→3.4.0 in about 50 minutes), right after the 'contract freezes' promise. Every ^5 install picks each one up automatically: five Renovate/Dependabot PRs, five CJS size bumps, five release notes about niche DTE features. That reads as 'rut.ts is becoming a DTE library and still moving fast', which is the opposite of what wins over users of the unmaintained leaders.
- **It assumes every issue deserves an API.** The analyses say three of the five should be docs-only and one should be deferred.
- **The budget ends up choosing for you.** Measured headroom is about 192 B ESM / 186 B CJS. Whichever issue merges first effectively decides the others; for example, #46 alone leaves 14 B ESM and 3 B CJS.
- **Each release costs the full ceremony.** A release PR, tag, GitHub Release and www-rut.ts sync each time multiplies the risk that the docs site drifts.
- **Thin releases do not build momentum.** A trickle of small niche releases creates news fatigue, not interest.
- **The upside is small.** Isolation and bisectability are the main benefit, and they matter little for independent, additive exports.
strategies.case_against_single_big_release:
- **It ties safe work to unsettled work.** It couples zero-code docs fixes and one proven, low-risk export (#47) with heuristic APIs whose details are unresolved: the #45 ranges, the #46 grammar, and the #44 list. Either the urgent guidance fixes wait months on implementation, or the heuristics are rushed and frozen permanently, with no pre-release channel to catch mistakes.
- **It breaks the size budget.** All five together cost roughly +450–550 B brotli, which would force the core caps up to about 2.3–2.4 kB (+25%). That weakens the 'tiny' claim, and the bundlejs badge, which measures with treeshake=[*], would grow. CJS consumers would pay all of it automatically through ^5.
- **It undermines the freeze message.** Shipping the largest API addition in the library's history about four months after the 'final-shape' major tells evaluators that v5 was not final, and it maximizes regret if anything is wrong.
- **It is harder to review and to explain.** One giant release note buries the trust messages. Review, mutation testing and the docs-site sync all get harder.
- **The issues would not ship as written anyway.** Four of the five issue specs are rejected or reshaped by the analyses, so 'ship them all together' would really mean shipping something nobody has fully specified.
cross_issue_decisions_needed_first: Closed-options policy: no new options on validate(), isValidRut() or ValidateOptions for all of 5.x, and the calculateVerifier floor stays. This settles #44 (allowSiiPlaceholders, strict:'sii') and #48 (minBodyLength, allowShortBody) together, and should be written publicly in the 5.0.1 README and CHANGELOG.

Demand threshold for new frozen API (#44, #45, #46). Recommended: an issue or PR from outside arrowsw, or a shipped dte-sdk code path where the userland version proved insufficient. dte-sdk's plans alone do not count; it is 0.0.2 with a hello() placeholder and no rut.ts dependency.

Size-budget policy. Keep the core caps at 1.9/2.0 kB and record the measured baseline (1708 B ESM / 1814 B CJS from the challengers' builds). Anything that does not fit either waits or goes to a subpath with its own size-limit entry. Decide now whether subpaths are acceptable at all, since each exports-map entry is itself frozen.

Scope boundary between rut.ts and dte-sdk. SII data and rules live in dte-sdk: SII_RUT 60803000-K, generic-receiver constants, RUTRecep / 135 UF / CdgIntRecep rules, the per-document SII floors, and the XSD-exact pattern. rut.ts only documents them and links to SII.
A single naming convention for exported constants and scanner verbs, decided before RUT_PATTERN freezes. Every later constant inherits it.

Source policy for regulatory facts in docs: primary SII documents opened by a person, with the access date. No search-engine snippets and no LLM-authored transcriptions. This applies to #44, #45 and #48 content in 5.0.1.
Whether to pledge the 7–8 digit body explicitly as part of the frozen contract. Recommended: yes, as a 'Clarified' note in the 5.0.1 CHANGELOG entry, without editing the released 5.0.0 entry.

Error and input conventions for any future API. No new error classes (no RangeError) without an explicit decision. Non-string handling follows the existing split: predicates return false, and string helpers throw by default and honor throwOnError.

Release cadence rule, written into RELEASING.md: at most one minor every 4–6 weeks; never more than one release on the same day except a hotfix; docs-only patches allowed; release notes in English and Spanish.

Triage of the maintainer-authored issues. Recommended: keep #44, #45 and #46 open with a needs-demand or incubating label and a written decision comment, so that outside +1s become the measurable demand signal. Close #48 when 5.0.1 ships.
naming_and_consistency_rules: Data constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE in a singular namespace style (RUT_PATTERN.any, RUT_PATTERN.hyphen). Any future constant set follows the same rule. They are plain literals: no Object.freeze, no RegExp objects.
Exported strings are frozen byte-for-byte, because consumers persist them in migrations, OpenAPI documents and snapshots. Typing them as literals is fine, and hover then shows the regex.

Functions are camelCase and start with a verb. Predicates are is*: they take unknown, return boolean and never throw. A future text scanner uses find*/scan*, never 'extract', because the docs already use 'extract' for getBody/getVerifier.

Reuse the existing option names (requireValid, throwOnError, strict, format, count, bodyLength). Boolean options default to the safer behavior. No numeric knobs that allow invalid states (hence no minBodyLength).

Identifiers and string-literal values are English, lowercase where applicable, in the style of GenerateFormat ('dotted' | 'compact' | 'hyphen'). No Spanish identifiers such as 'juridica'; Spanish terms appear only in docs.

There is one shape contract. Anything that accepts or emits RUT strings agrees with validate(): 7–8 digit body, [1-9] lead digit, no leading zeros, uppercase K on output, and compact normalized output matching clean().
Anti-PII: never echo input. Any throw is an InvalidRutError with the constant message 'Invalid RUT input'. Docs flag outputs that contain RUTs (and generate() output) as potential personal data.
Only isValidRut mints the branded Rut type. Do not export a type that merely describes a constant; typeof is enough.
Subpaths, if ever used, are lowercase nouns ('rut.ts/text'), each with its own size-limit entry, and are documented as frozen surface.
risks: The plan may look thin next to feature-rich competitors. @rut-toolkit/core has classification, placeholders, barcodes and error codes. Mitigation: compete on trust and DTE correctness through a dated comparison page, Spanish docs, migration guides, and a published needs-demand list that invites +1s.
A docs-only 5.0.1 makes every ^5 user get a Renovate/Dependabot PR that changes no code. Mitigation: a clear 'no code changes' note; 4.0.1 set the precedent.

Inaccurate SII facts in the README would damage a library whose brand is trust. Much of the research came from search snippets because sii.cl was unreachable. Mitigation: the primary-source gate on 5.0.1.

Publicly declining or deferring four of the owner's own issues could read as indecision. Mitigation: written rationale on each issue, framed like the parse() precedent from #36, and keeping them open for outside demand.
After 5.1, about 110–140 B of core headroom remains (an estimate; measure it). Any later feature forces a subpath or a cap raise, and a subpath is itself new frozen surface.

RUT_PATTERN strings are permanent. If the docs on mobile-number false positives (any/compact), JS-only trim equivalence and MySQL _ci collations are weak, users will misuse the patterns as validators.

Ley 21.719 (in force 2026-12-01 unless boletín 18.623-07 postpones it to December 2027) creates a window in which a competitor may ship a redaction helper first. Mitigation: a 5.0.1 docs recipe built on mask() and non-echoing errors. This is acceptable compared with freezing an unproven grammar.
Docs drift. RELEASING.md's step after publishing (the www-rut.ts sync) is easy to skip, and a bilingual README doubles the maintenance. A stale docs site costs more trust than a missing feature.

Duplication with dte-sdk. The SII constants and the extraction prototype living in dte-sdk could diverge from the rut.ts docs. Mitigation: dte-sdk imports rut.ts for all RUT logic and owns only SII data and rules.
Cadence credibility. If 5.1.0 slips well past its target, or ends up on the same day as another release, the 'calm cadence' message weakens. 5.0.1 carries the narrative either way.
strategies.bottom_line: Don't do either option. Ship two releases, a few weeks apart. First, a docs-only 5.0.1 now with byte-identical code. It carries the decisions on #44, #45 and #48, the clean()-on-text warning from #46, the strict vs plain validate() guidance for SII documents, and Spanish npm metadata. Second, a 5.1.0 that adds only #47's proven RUT_PATTERN, within the current size caps. #46 waits for incubation in dte-sdk and for real demand; if it ever ships, it goes alone as a subpath minor. The #44 and #45 APIs join parse() on a public needs-demand list. #48's minBodyLength, and any other new validate() option, is declined for all of 5.x. rut.ts has about 228 weekly downloads, its strength is trust, and its history is churn, so what wins adopters is a calm, predictable release cadence and docs that answer Chilean developers' real questions, not more frozen API. dte-sdk loses nothing: it is pre-alpha, needs only functions rut.ts already has, and should own the SII-specific data.

strategies.lens: Engineering sequencing: how the issues depend on each other, which decisions have to be settled before any code ships, whether prereleases help, and what dte-sdk needs first versus later. I checked the release pipeline (RELEASING.md, publish.yml, ci.yml, .size-limit.json, postbuild.mjs) and the state of dte-sdk (0.0.2: a hello() placeholder with no rut.ts dependency). The 2 kB CJS cap is the one that binds first.

Values are backslash-free, anchored, [1-9]/[0-9]/[.] strings proven equal to isRutLike after JS trim (raw length ≤ 64). It is a plain object of string primitives typed with readonly members: no Object.freeze, no RegExp objects. Each string is frozen byte-for-byte for v5.
No RUT_JSON_SCHEMA export and no SII/XSD pattern. The JSON Schema one-liner goes in the README; the XSD-exact RUTType belongs in dte-sdk.

validate()/parseRutLike internals are untouched. I measured deriving the internal regexes from the exported strings: it saves only 10 B ESM and 0 B CJS (1784/1901 vs 1794/1897), so it is not worth touching the frozen gate.

README section 'Schema patterns (JSON Schema / OpenAPI / SQL)' covering: shape only, always pair with validate(); `any` and `compact` accept any 9-digit mobile number (~1/11 even pass Modulo 11), so prefer `hyphen`/`dotted` in API schemas; a Zod snippet with .regex() before any transform plus z.toJSONSchema(..., { io: 'input' }); equivalence holds for JS trim only; engine notes (Python fullmatch, PHP /D, Ruby \A\z, strip anchors for XSD, never add g/y/i); a MySQL _ci collation caveat for storage CHECKs. releases.rationale: #47 is the only issue whose API adds no new frozen semantics. It has general, non-DTE demand: z.toJSONSchema drops .refine() but keeps .regex(). Measured cost with the repo toolchain is +86 B ESM / +83 B CJS for all four strings (1794 / 1897 B), or +61/+62 for `any` alone. It fits, but it uses about 45% of the remaining headroom. That is consistent with deferring those, but it has to be an explicit decision. Measurement scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dte-sdk/fc9ade2f-319c-5a08-b848-6a95c60c3cdb/scratchpad/agents/release-seq/gen.mjs, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dte-sdk/fc9ade2f-319c-5a08-b848-6a95c60c3cdb/scratchpad/agents/release-seq/gen2.mjs, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dte-sdk/fc9ade2f-319c-5a08-b848-6a95c60c3cdb/scratchpad/agents/release-seq/min.mjs. releases.version: 5.2.0+ (unscheduled; only when a demand trigger fires; batched by theme, not by issue)
contents: Possible 'text' theme: #46 as findRuts/scanRuts on a `rut.ts/text` subpath with its own size-limit entry. Positions, requireValid, explicit boundaries, no lookbehind, linear time, deliberate non-string handling.
Possible 'fixtures' theme: #45 generate({ kind }) with gap-aware 'typical' ranges (person well below ~30M, entity ≥ 60M) and no RangeError, or a defined precedence instead.
Possible 'generic RUTs' theme: #44 isGenericRut, only once a closed, primary-sourced list policy exists (the set already has at least 5 SII-named values).
Possible later: parse()/reason codes (#36) or a Standard Schema object, under the same rule.
releases.rationale: Nothing here has demand from outside arrowsw today. Every rut.ts issue was filed by the maintainer, and dte-sdk is a placeholder that does not need these. Each item freezes a data list, a numeric threshold or a heuristic grammar that the evidence says may need correcting. None of them fits in the core file after #47. Batching by theme stops merge order from deciding how the byte budget gets spent.

issues_not_shipped.disposition: Docs only (5.0.1). API deferred (needs-demand). The validate() allowance is rejected. SII_RUT and the receiver constants move to dte-sdk.
issues_not_shipped.reason: Rejected outright: `allowSiiPlaceholders` is a relaxation flag that CHANGELOG 5.0.0 forbids ('flag-free (except strict)'). `strict: boolean | 'sii'` breaks consumer types (TS2345, reproduced on TS 5.9.3). A shape-agnostic isSiiPlaceholder reopens the zero-padding hole: `strict || isPh` accepts '066666666-6'. 60803000-K is the SII's real RUT, and its carátula role is a DTE rule. The optional GENERIC_RUTS/isGenericRut is deferred for three reasons. The set is open: SII documents also name 33.333.333-3 and 77.777.777-7, and under the freeze adding an entry later changes behaviour. A two-line userland recipe matches the canonical predicate on every edge case. It costs +108 B ESM / +119 B CJS that the core no longer has after #47.

issues_not_shipped.disposition: Docs only plus contract tests (5.0.1). minBodyLength rejected. A calculateVerifier allowShortBody opt-in is 'not planned'. dte-sdk chooses its own SII floor policy.
issues_not_shipped.reason: Option (2) is a relaxation flag on validate()/isValidRut, and since they share ValidateOptions it would also put the Rut brand on short strings. On decompose() it relaxes the shared lenient core: decompose('Folio 77') would return {7,7}. It breaks mask() for 5- or 6-digit bodies (PII exposure) and costs about 100–140 B that cannot be tree-shaken. The calculateVerifier-only opt-in breaks the tested coherence law that any body calculateVerifier accepts produces a validate()-passing RUT, and userland Modulo 11 is about 8 lines. SII itself uses three different floors (XSD none, Reclamo WS reportedly 1000, Formato DTE 100.000), so the policy belongs in dte-sdk.

strategies.case_against_one_minor_per_issue: Only one of the five issues (#47) justifies new API now. #48 is a question that resolves to docs. #44 and #45 resolve to docs plus a rejection or deferral. #46 should be deferred. A minor per issue would either push deferred or rejected designs into frozen API to fill the queue, or produce empty minors. The issues are also tightly coupled. #44 and #48 both depend on the 'ValidateOptions is closed' policy. #46 and #47 share a grammar. #44 and #45 both run into the generic-RUT problem (kindOf('66666666-6') returns 'juridica'). Deciding them one release at a time risks a different naming and error convention frozen in each minor. The byte budget is shared and small: 192 B ESM / 186 B CJS measured. Releasing per issue means whichever issue merges first wins the budget (#46 alone takes 178 B), so allocation follows merge order rather than value. Each release costs a release PR, a tag, a GitHub Release and a www-rut.ts sync, so five releases mean five chances for the docs site to drift. A run of minors would also recall the five 3.x releases cut within about 50 minutes, which undercuts the stability promise the 5.0 freeze was meant to signal.
strategies.case_against_single_big_release: The cheapest recommended form of each feature does not fit. #47 +86, #44 API +108, #45 kind +52–89 and #46 +178 add up to about 424–461 B ESM against 192 B of headroom. Shipping it all means raising the caps or introducing subpaths, and those structural, irreversible packaging decisions would be made under release pressure. A big release ties zero-risk corrective docs (the clean() embedded-text hazard, the wrong '7–8 digits' universal statement) to high-risk, irreversible API that lacks demand (#45, #46) or still has open research (#44's list is incomplete; #46's grammar is untested on real text). The docs would wait on the slowest API review. It would freeze about a dozen permanent decisions in one review, against the #36 precedent: parse() was dropped, despite 41 passing tests, because the freeze makes additions irreversible. And it makes bisecting differential-harness or Stryker regressions harder.
cross_issue_decisions_needed_first: ValidateOptions stays closed for all of v5 as { strict?: boolean }: no allowance flags, no minBodyLength, no union widening of strict. This also covers isValidRut and any future function that might forward options to validate (extract must not forward strict). It settles #44 and #48 together.

Admission rule for new exports under the freeze. Only add things that (a) re-express the already-frozen contract or Modulo 11 math, (b) are closed, primary-sourced data, or (c) are requested by at least one consumer outside arrowsw. dte-sdk alone does not count, because it would steer a general library from a sibling project. Data lists, numeric thresholds and heuristic grammars count as frozen behaviour once shipped.

Byte-budget policy, decided before 5.1.0 so #47 doesn't settle it implicitly. Measured headroom is 192 B ESM / 186 B CJS, with CJS binding first. Core caps stay at 1.9/2 kB. The core takes #47 (+86/+83 B) and nothing else in 5.x. Later features go to a subpath with its own size-limit entry, or do not ship. Raising core caps needs an explicit maintainer decision, not a side effect of some PR.
Exported-constant conventions (shape, naming, typing). Settle these now because every constant freezes together.
Output convention for any function that returns RUTs: canonical compact (clean() form, uppercase K) as a plain string, never the branded Rut. isValidRut stays the only way to mint a Rut.

Error and input conventions for new functions: only InvalidRutError with the constant non-echoing message, no new RangeError or TypeError. Predicates over unknown return false. String-taking helpers throw by default and honour throwOnError. Never return a silent [] or null on non-string input where that would hide data (the redaction case).

Body range: the 7–8 digit body with no leading zero is stated as part of the frozen contract (in the 5.0.1 CHANGELOG 'Clarified' entry). Every new API (patterns, any future scanner or generator option) inherits it. No parameterized pattern builders.

rut.ts and dte-sdk boundary. dte-sdk owns: SII_RUT 60803000-K for the carátula, the generic-receiver constants and their DTE conditions (135 UF, RUTRecep='0' with CdgIntRecep), the XSD-exact RUTType check with its own Modulo 11 and its reception-vs-emission floor policy, kind-aware fixtures, and any incubating text scanner. rut.ts owns only role-free RUT facts.

Release mechanics: release when a theme is ready, not on a calendar. Docs-only patches are allowed when dist min.js is byte-identical. No two releases on the same day. No prerelease channel for now. If one is ever needed, publish.yml must first map tags containing '-' to `npm publish --tag next`; today it passes no --tag, so a v5.1.0-beta.0 tag would either land on `latest` or be refused, depending on the npm version, and each beta would also need its own release PR.
naming_and_consistency_rules: Data constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and are exported as plain object literals of string primitives with explicitly typed readonly members. No Object.freeze: esbuild keeps the call and terser strips /*#__PURE__*/. No exported RegExp objects, because of lastIndex and flag state.
Exported string values are frozen byte-for-byte for v5, even though the .d.ts types them as `string`. Consumers persist them in migrations and OpenAPI documents, and diff tools flag any respelling.
Shape keys reuse the existing GenerateFormat literals exactly ('compact' | 'hyphen' | 'dotted'), plus 'any'. No new synonyms such as 'canonical' or 'withHyphen'.

Name for #47: `RUT_PATTERN`. It is singular, after the JSON Schema `pattern` keyword the values feed, and the issue already uses it. Whatever is chosen, any later data constant follows the same singular `RUT_*` prefix rule.

Option names reuse existing vocabulary: requireValid (from equals), throwOnError (SafeOptions), format: GenerateFormat, bodyLength. No option may share a name with an exported function (so no `validate` option). Opt-ins are booleans, never numeric knobs such as minBodyLength.
Function names: camelCase verbs. Predicates start with is*. A free-text scanner would be find*/scan*, never 'extract', because the docs already use 'extract' for getBody/getVerifier.
Enum values are in English (no 'juridica'). No DTE-role names (RECEIVER, CARATULA, CONSUMIDOR_FINAL) anywhere in rut.ts's public surface.
Every new export ships in the same release with: JSDoc, a README section, an llms.txt entry, expect-type tests, a typeof-agnostic dist smoke-test entry, a CHANGELOG entry and a www-rut.ts page.
risks: Freeze irreversibility: a wrong RUT_PATTERN string in 5.1.0 is permanent until a v6 that is not planned. Mitigation: per-string exhaustive equivalence tests and compile checks under ''/u/v flags, rather than only the union test.

Implicit budget decision: after #47 only about 106 B ESM / 103 B CJS remain, which is too little for #44's API, #46, or most of #45. If the budget policy isn't recorded first, 5.1.0 silently decides those issues by bytes.

Regulatory facts in docs: much of the SII evidence came from search snippets or third-party transcriptions, because sii.cl was unreachable from the research sandbox. A reference library publishing a wrong SII rule loses trust. Mitigation: a human reads the primary sources, tables are dated, and anything unverified is cut.
Pressure from the sibling project: dte-sdk (same org) will keep 'needing' things. Without the external-demand rule, a general RUT library will pick up DTE-shaped API one minor at a time.

Perceived stagnation: four of five issues end as docs, deferred or rejected, and nothing has shipped since July. Mitigation: ship 5.0.1 promptly, post clear disposition comments, use a needs-demand label, and link recipes.
Release optics: 5.0.1 and 5.1.0 cut close together could echo the 3.x 50-minute burst. Keep them days apart, or fold them into one release.
Prerelease misfire: with the current publish.yml, a hand-pushed v5.1.0-beta.0 tag would run the publish job with no --tag.
A docs-only patch touches src JSDoc, which ships in the tarball. The min.js byte-identity gate guards against an accidental code change.
Misuse of #47: pattern-only schemas accept 9-digit mobile numbers, MySQL _ci collations make uppercase storage guards a no-op, and case-insensitive engines admit U+212A. Needs explicit docs.
Future subpath packaging: TS moduleResolution node10 can't see exports subpaths without typesVersions, and CJS/ESM/Deno resolution must be tested from a packed tarball before the first subpath ships.
Deferred prototypes (extract final.mjs, generate kind) may go stale, or a competitor ships something similar first. That is acceptable: additions can come in any 5.x minor, removals never.
strategies.bottom_line:
Use neither a minor per issue nor one big release. Cut two releases.

1. **5.0.1, docs and tests only, as soon as the sources are verified.** It carries the #48 body-range documentation, contract tests for inputs below the floor that have a valid DV, and the docs halves of #46 (clean() takes one value per string), #44 (generic SII RUTs) and #45 (person-or-entity heuristic and fixture recipe). The minified dist must be byte-identical to 5.0.0.
2. **5.1.0 with only #47 RUT_PATTERN.** It ships only after the cross-issue decisions are recorded: ValidateOptions stays closed, the admission rule for new exports, the byte-budget policy, and naming. Measured cost is +86 B ESM / +83 B CJS. validate() internals stay untouched, because deriving them from the exported strings saves only 10 B.

What does not ship:
- #44's validate() allowance and #45's kindOf() are rejected.
- #48's minBodyLength is rejected, and allowShortBody is not planned.
- #46 extract(), #45 generate({ kind }) and #44 isGenericRut are deferred until someone outside arrowsw asks. If they come back, they arrive as themed minors on subpaths, because the core file can't hold them after #47.

No prereleases. A beta would get no external testers, the exhaustive tests give stronger evidence, and publish.yml would first need changing to map prerelease tags to `--tag next`.

dte-sdk is not blocked by any of this. It can depend on rut.ts@^5.0.0 today: plain validate() for XML reception, and format(x, { dots: false }) for the SII form. It should own SII_RUT, the generic-receiver rules, its XSD floor policy, its fixtures and any text scanner, and upstream only what turns out to be generic and wanted by others.
